data_objects.name: subject_sensor_tables
data_objects.meaning: Fifteen per-subject CSV tables of combined, timestamped physiological-sensor signals. The inspected tables share the columns session, real_time, eda, hr, temp, and bvp.

data_objects.name: survey_results
data_objects.meaning: Interval-level survey records keyed by subject code, with start and end times, a duration and date, a coded stress level, and 13 context or stressor indicator fields.

variables.name: session
variables.meaning: Composite session code repeated across contiguous samples; sampled values combine the subject code and a numeric suffix separated by an underscore.

variables.name: real_time
variables.meaning: Numeric sample timestamp. Within inspected contiguous runs it advances by 0.25, and it jumps between sessions.
variables.unit: seconds (epoch-like reference; exact convention not stated)

variables.name: eda
variables.meaning: Electrodermal-activity signal value at the sample timestamp.

variables.name: hr
variables.meaning: Heart-rate signal value at the sample timestamp.

variables.name: temp
variables.meaning: Temperature signal value at the sample timestamp.

variables.name: bvp
variables.meaning: Blood-volume-pulse signal value at the sample timestamp.

variables.name: ID
variables.meaning: Subject code. Sampled values match the subject codes in sensor-table filenames and session prefixes.

variables.name: Start time
variables.meaning: Recorded start timestamp of the survey interval, formatted as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.

variables.name: End time
variables.meaning: Recorded end timestamp of the survey interval, formatted as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.

variables.name: Duration
variables.meaning: Recorded elapsed duration between the interval endpoints, formatted as HH:MM:SS.

variables.name: Date
variables.meaning: Recorded calendar date associated with the survey interval; sampled overnight rows show that it is not always the calendar-date component of Start time.

variables.name: Stress level
variables.meaning: Coded stress-level value; sampled rows contain 0, 1, and 2, but their category labels are not declared in the inspected files.

structure.description: Each subject_sensor_tables row is one combined sensor sample within one session. The inspected contiguous runs are locally ordered by real_time at 0.25-second steps, while session boundaries introduce time gaps.

Each survey_results row represents one time interval for one subject code, accompanied by a stress-level code and context indicators. Survey file order is not reliably chronological in the sampled regions.

The apparent cross-object subject link is survey_results.ID to the code in each sensor filename and the prefix of subject_sensor_tables.session. Time fields may support interval alignment, but no explicit sensor-session foreign key is present.

uncertainties: The inspected CSVs contain no embedded data dictionary. Units, calibration, preprocessing, interpolation, and missing-value conventions for eda, hr, temp, and bvp are not stated.
real_time has epoch-like magnitude and quarter-second increments, but its epoch, time zone, and exact relation to the timezone-free survey timestamps are not declared.
The numeric suffix in session resembles a time value, and sampled sessions begin about 10 seconds after that suffix, but the suffix's formal definition is not stated.
The meanings and ordering of Stress level codes 0, 1, and 2 are not defined in the inspected files, so no verbal class labels are assigned.
The 13 survey indicator columns are 0/1 in sampled rows, but the files do not define whether 1 means selected, present, causal, or something else, nor whether other codes or blanks occur elsewhere.
The Date field can differ from the date component of Start time for overnight records; it may represent a reporting date, shift date, or another convention that is not documented in the files.

No unique survey-row key is declared. Sampled survey rows include the same ID, start time, end time, and duration more than once with a differing indicator, so those fields should not be assumed to form a unique key.

The subject-code and temporal relationships between the sensor and survey objects are inferred from matching values and formats; alignment rules and intended interval boundaries are not supplied in the inspected files.

Content checks were deliberately bounded to representative rows and regions, so schema consistency, value domains, ordering, and data-quality behavior were not exhaustively profiled across roughly 18 million lines.
annotation_notes: Scope was limited to the 16 CSV files in the permitted prepared/public directory: 15 subject sensor tables and survey_results.csv.

The public inventory and line counts were checked, then rows were sampled from the beginnings, interiors, session transitions, and ends of representative numeric- and alphabetic-code subject files; survey_results.csv was sampled at its beginning, middle, and end.
All variable names preserve source capitalization, spacing, and spelling, including Ancilliary services.
For sensor variables, file is null because the variable applies across the grouped 15-file data object; the concrete relative paths are enumerated in that object's files list.
This is a task-independent semantic map: it describes available objects, row grains, fields, and apparent links without selecting a prediction target or imposing downstream label semantics.
